repositories.name: claude-token-saver-mcp
repositories.catalog_section: Agent runtimes, routing, and workflow orchestration
repositories.summary: Routes routine generation, tests, summaries, and simple refactors from Claude Code to local Ollama models, with cloud fallback and a cost dashboard.
repositories.mechanism: Routes routine generation, tests, summaries, and simple refactors from Claude Code to local Ollama models, with cloud fallback and a cost dashboard.
repositories.reported_result: No independently reviewed benchmark; README estimates savings from offloading a portion of routine requests.
repositories.main_caveat: This reduces premium cloud-token use, not necessarily total tokens or compute; local-model quality varies by task.

repositories.name: cc_token_saver_mcp
repositories.catalog_section: Agent runtimes, routing, and workflow orchestration
repositories.summary: A small MCP server that exposes a local OpenAI-compatible model for simple Claude Code tasks while retaining Claude for complex coordination.
repositories.mechanism: A small MCP server that exposes a local OpenAI-compatible model for simple Claude Code tasks while retaining Claude for complex coordination.
repositories.reported_result: No quantified benchmark was reviewed.
repositories.main_caveat: Experimental and narrowly documented; routing quality depends on Claude choosing the local tools appropriately.

repositories.name: vix
repositories.catalog_section: Agent runtimes, routing, and workflow orchestration
repositories.summary: A coding agent that reuses prompt cache across phases with stem agents and exposes a Tree-sitter virtual filesystem containing minified code.
repositories.mechanism: A coding agent that reuses prompt cache across phases with stem agents and exposes a Tree-sitter virtual filesystem containing minified code.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer reports 20–50% fewer code-reading tokens and a seven-task cost comparison of $6.64 versus $12.44 for Claude Code, with transcripts published.
repositories.main_caveat: The maintainers explicitly call the benchmark observational rather than scientific; one task was slightly more expensive.

repositories.name: tokless
repositories.catalog_section: Agent runtimes, routing, and workflow orchestration
repositories.summary: A cross-platform installer and lifecycle manager that wires RTK, Caveman, CodeGraph, and Context Mode into several coding agents as a preselected token-saving stack.
repositories.mechanism: A cross-platform installer and lifecycle manager that wires RTK, Caveman, CodeGraph, and Context Mode into several coding agents as a preselected token-saving stack.
repositories.reported_result: No independent aggregate benchmark is supplied; the README repeats component-level examples from the bundled projects.
repositories.main_caveat: It adds no new compression algorithm and inherits the compatibility, licensing, overlap, and benchmark limitations of four separate tools; stack-level attribution is difficult.

repositories.name: cavekit
repositories.catalog_section: Agent runtimes, routing, and workflow orchestration
repositories.summary: A compressed spec-driven Claude Code workflow using one durable SPEC.md, right-sized ceremony, no subagents in the current version, and compact caveman encoding for persistent task state.
repositories.mechanism: A compressed spec-driven Claude Code workflow using one durable SPEC.md, right-sized ceremony, no subagents in the current version, and compact caveman encoding for persistent task state.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer reports all nine skill descriptions consume about 1.1K context tokens, described as 16× lighter than spec-kit, and caveman-encoded prose is roughly 75% smaller.
repositories.main_caveat: The comparison is configuration-level, not an end-to-end task benchmark; a durable spec can still become stale or add overhead on small changes.

repositories.name: claude-code-token-saver
repositories.catalog_section: Agent runtimes, routing, and workflow orchestration
repositories.summary: Claude Code plugin with cache-expiry protection, subtask delegation, concise mode, session continuation, usage reporting, and lighter Git operations.
repositories.mechanism: Claude Code plugin with cache-expiry protection, subtask delegation, concise mode, session continuation, usage reporting, and lighter Git operations.
repositories.reported_result: README claims a measured 45% cost reduction.
repositories.main_caveat: The reviewed README did not establish independent replication or a broad benchmark suite.

repositories.name: kevin-mode
repositories.summary: A Claude Code skill that removes action narration, repeated summaries, filler transitions, and obvious status updates while keeping code, questions, warnings, and non-obvious reasoning.
repositories.mechanism: A Claude Code skill that removes action narration, repeated summaries, filler transitions, and obvious status updates while keeping code, questions, warnings, and non-obvious reasoning.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer projects 35–45% lower net output, including 60–70% less prose and no reduction in code tokens.
repositories.main_caveat: The figures are projections rather than a published measured benchmark, and the skill does not address input, reasoning, or tool-output tokens.

repositories.name: oafish
repositories.summary: A cross-agent terse-response skill whose Claude Code hook also digests verbose Read, Bash, and MCP results before they fill context.
repositories.mechanism: A cross-agent terse-response skill whose Claude Code hook also digests verbose Read, Bash, and MCP results before they fill context.
repositories.reported_result: README claims about 75% fewer output tokens and ships a live-model benchmark harness, but no completed aggregate benchmark results were reviewed.
repositories.main_caveat: The headline is not supported by published aggregate results in the reviewed README; digesting tool outputs can omit diagnostics and should retain a raw fallback.

repositories.name: whippet
repositories.summary: A Claude Code minimal-code and safety discipline that prefers reuse, standard-library and native features, preserves validation and security, leaves runnable checks, and reports briefly.
repositories.mechanism: A Claude Code minimal-code and safety discipline that prefers reuse, standard-library and native features, preserves validation and security, leaves runnable checks, and reports briefly.
repositories.reported_result: In a 13-task Opus 4.8 screen, the maintainer reports little code-size or dependency reduction versus baseline, but more persistent runnable checks and additional trust-boundary validation.
repositories.main_caveat: The evaluation is small, one run per cell, and does not demonstrate token savings on the tested strong model; its value is primarily workflow discipline rather than proven cost reduction.

repositories.name: ponytail
repositories.summary: A cross-agent minimal-code discipline that applies YAGNI, standard-library and native-feature preference, dependency reuse, and explicit safety exceptions before generating code.
repositories.mechanism: A cross-agent minimal-code discipline that applies YAGNI, standard-library and native-feature preference, dependency reuse, and explicit safety exceptions before generating code.
repositories.reported_result: On twelve feature tasks with Haiku 4.5 and four runs per arm, the maintainer reports 54% fewer added lines, 22% fewer total tokens, 20% lower cost, and 27% less time, with 100% safety on a separate adversarial tier.
repositories.main_caveat: Results are model- and task-specific; gains concentrate in over-build traps and approach zero on irreducible work. The maintainer notes some reasoning models can spend more tokens under the discipline.

repositories.name: caveman
repositories.summary: A cross-agent skill and plugin that suppresses filler, hedging, narration, and repeated summaries; companion commands also compress persistent instruction files and MCP descriptions.
repositories.mechanism: A cross-agent skill and plugin that suppresses filler, hedging, narration, and repeated summaries; companion commands also compress persistent instruction files and MCP descriptions.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer reports an average 65% output-token reduction across ten prompts. Ponytail's separate agentic benchmark found Caveman used 7% more total tokens on twelve feature tasks despite producing less code.
repositories.main_caveat: It primarily changes model output, not reasoning or tool-input tokens. Lower response verbosity may have little or negative effect on total-session cost when deliberation and tool use dominate. Fresh pinned source-logic inspection is available; benchmark-audit and reproduction remain required before measured savings or deployment-grade recommendation.

repositories.name: scrooge-mode
repositories.summary: A bilingual Korean/English output-compression skill with reinjection hooks, safety auto-clarity, token statistics, and language-specific terse registers.
repositories.mechanism: A bilingual Korean/English output-compression skill with reinjection hooks, safety auto-clarity, token statistics, and language-specific terse registers.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer reports paired-median output reductions near 70% for Korean and 73% for English on Claude Opus 4.8, with held-out cross-checks near 71% and 68%.
repositories.main_caveat: The main evaluation uses one run per prompt and replaces the normal Claude Code system prompt to isolate register effects; real sessions may differ and only output tokens are measured.

repositories.name: concise
repositories.summary: A cross-agent response-style skill that removes filler and hedging while preserving conventional English grammar and allows one-turn elaboration before returning to concise mode.
repositories.mechanism: A cross-agent response-style skill that removes filler and hedging while preserving conventional English grammar and allows one-turn elaboration before returning to concise mode.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer claims roughly 60–70% fewer output tokens and provides before-and-after examples, but no reviewed task-level benchmark was found.
repositories.main_caveat: The claim is output-only and example-based; it does not measure reasoning, tool calls, total session tokens, or answer-quality regressions.

repositories.name: Bonsai
repositories.summary: A cross-agent YAGNI and minimal-code plugin that prefers existing, standard-library, native, and installed solutions and preserves safety-critical validation and accessibility.
repositories.mechanism: A cross-agent YAGNI and minimal-code plugin that prefers existing, standard-library, native, and installed solutions and preserves safety-critical validation and accessibility.
repositories.reported_result: A correctness-gated benchmark harness is present, but the README states that paid benchmark numbers have not yet been published.
repositories.main_caveat: No completed token, cost, or latency results were available during review; it is conceptually close to Ponytail and should be evaluated for incremental rather than duplicated value.

repositories.name: ast-bro
repositories.summary: AST outlines, dependency/call graphs, semantic search, blast-radius analysis, token-budgeted context packs, and reversible log squeezing.
repositories.mechanism: AST outlines, dependency/call graphs, semantic search, blast-radius analysis, token-budgeted context packs, and reversible log squeezing.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer reports typical outline savings near 95% versus reading full files and bounded context packs for multi-hop analysis.
repositories.main_caveat: Static analysis is language- and parser-dependent; generated context should not replace exact source inspection before edits.

repositories.name: aider
repositories.summary: A coding agent with a repository map that summarizes the codebase so larger projects can be navigated without loading every file.
repositories.mechanism: A coding agent with a repository map that summarizes the codebase so larger projects can be navigated without loading every file.
repositories.reported_result: No token-saving percentage was reviewed in the repository README; the repo-map mechanism is explicitly designed for scalable context selection.
repositories.main_caveat: A full coding agent rather than a drop-in optimization layer.

repositories.name: tokensave
repositories.summary: Builds a local semantic knowledge graph with symbol search, callers/callees, context bundles, impact analysis, and agent hooks that redirect wasteful reads.
repositories.mechanism: Builds a local semantic knowledge graph with symbol search, callers/callees, context bundles, impact analysis, and agent hooks that redirect wasteful reads.
repositories.reported_result: No single end-to-end reduction figure was reviewed; the project explicitly targets fewer file scans, tool calls, and context tokens.
repositories.main_caveat: Large tool manifests and broad feature sets can create overhead unless the agent uses the compact paths consistently.

repositories.name: cocoindex-code
repositories.summary: AST-based semantic code indexing and targeted search exposed through a CLI, skill, or MCP server.
repositories.mechanism: AST-based semantic code indexing and targeted search exposed through a CLI, skill, or MCP server.
repositories.reported_result: README advertises approximately 70% instant token savings from targeted semantic search.
repositories.main_caveat: The reviewed README did not provide the full methodology behind the headline percentage. Fresh pinned source-logic inspection is available; benchmark-audit and reproduction remain required before measured savings or deployment-grade recommendation.

repositories.name: graphify
repositories.summary: Turns folders of code, database schemas, infrastructure, documents, images, and videos into a queryable knowledge graph for AI coding assistants.
repositories.mechanism: Graphify is a Python CLI/skill package that builds `graphify-out/graph.json` from source/document corpora, installs host-specific agent skills/instructions, serves graph queries over MCP, and can keep graphs fresh via git hooks/watch/update paths. Source inspection supports a source-logic finding for mechanism and integration behavior, not measured token savings.
repositories.reported_result: GitHub repository metadata and README/package metadata describe Graphify as a queryable knowledge graph for code and adjacent project artifacts; no token-savings benchmark has been audited here yet.
repositories.main_caveat: Source-code logic has been inspected for representative mechanism, integration, state, and failure behavior; benchmark-audit and reproduction evidence remain required before measured savings or deployment-grade recommendations.

repositories.name: codegraph
repositories.summary: A local semantic code graph that lets agents query symbols, relationships, callers, and architecture instead of repeatedly scanning source with grep and full-file reads.
repositories.mechanism: A local semantic code graph that lets agents query symbols, relationships, callers, and architecture instead of repeatedly scanning source with grep and full-file reads.
repositories.reported_result: Across seven open-source codebases, the maintainer reports median results of 47% fewer total tokens, 58% fewer tool calls, 22% less time, and 16% lower cost, using four runs per arm.
repositories.main_caveat: The benchmark tests architecture questions rather than implementation tasks, is maintainer-run, and depends on graph accuracy and agent adoption of the MCP tools.

repositories.name: cachebro
repositories.summary: Caches file reads and returns one-line unchanged notices or compact diffs on later reads instead of resending full files.
repositories.mechanism: Caches file reads and returns one-line unchanged notices or compact diffs on later reads instead of resending full files.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer A/B test reports 26% fewer tokens on one refactoring task and about 24% over a three-task sequence.
repositories.main_caveat: Benefits are highest in sessions that reread the same files; token estimation is character-based and approximate.

repositories.name: toktoken
repositories.summary: Indexes symbols and imports, supports targeted retrieval, outlines, dependency tracing, compact JSON, and token-budget-aware result slicing.
repositories.mechanism: Indexes symbols and imports, supports targeted retrieval, outlines, dependency tracing, compact JSON, and token-budget-aware result slicing.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer examples on Redis and Linux report roughly 88–99% fewer tokens for targeted symbol retrieval than full-file reads.
repositories.main_caveat: Depends on Universal Ctags plus custom parsers; static-call and import analysis can be incomplete in dynamic code.

repositories.name: serena
repositories.summary: Symbol-level retrieval, references, refactoring, editing, diagnostics, and memory via language servers or a JetBrains backend.
repositories.mechanism: Symbol-level retrieval, references, refactoring, editing, diagnostics, and memory via language servers or a JetBrains backend.
repositories.reported_result: README describes symbolic editing and retrieval as more token-efficient than full-file and search/replace workflows; no single token benchmark was reviewed.
repositories.main_caveat: Primary goal is semantic IDE capability, not token reduction alone; efficiency varies with language-server quality and tool usage. Fresh pinned source-logic inspection is available; benchmark-audit and reproduction remain required before measured savings or deployment-grade recommendation.

repositories.name: qmd
repositories.summary: Local BM25, vector, and reranked search over documentation and knowledge collections with line-bounded retrieval for agents.
repositories.mechanism: Local BM25, vector, and reranked search over documentation and knowledge collections with line-bounded retrieval for agents.
repositories.reported_result: agentic-token-bench reports a 99.2% reduction on its pinned QMD retrieval tasks versus the raw artifacts.
repositories.main_caveat: QMD is primarily for markup/documents; code support depends on what is indexed and how documents are prepared.

repositories.name: codegraph-mcp
repositories.summary: Persistent code graph, session memory, learning, symbol navigation, and Bash-output compression in a Rust MCP server.
repositories.mechanism: Persistent code graph, session memory, learning, symbol navigation, and Bash-output compression in a Rust MCP server.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer reports 23% fewer tokens on a multi-step refactoring task in compact mode and much larger per-query reductions.
repositories.main_caveat: The README contains a stale clone command pointing at a different owner; compact-mode discipline materially affects results.

repositories.name: CornMCP
repositories.summary: MCP code intelligence with AST queries, semantic memory, quality gates, multi-agent awareness, and token-savings analytics.
repositories.mechanism: MCP code intelligence with AST queries, semantic memory, quality gates, multi-agent awareness, and token-savings analytics.
repositories.reported_result: No quantified benchmark was reviewed; the documented design avoids full-file dumps and tracks estimated savings.
repositories.main_caveat: A larger multi-service stack than single-purpose retrieval tools; operational overhead may outweigh benefits for small repositories.

repositories.name: headroom
repositories.summary: A local context-compression library, proxy, agent wrapper, and MCP server that routes JSON, code, prose, logs, files, and history through specialized compressors while caching originals for retrieval.
repositories.mechanism: A local context-compression library, proxy, agent wrapper, and MCP server that routes JSON, code, prose, logs, files, and history through specialized compressors while caching originals for retrieval.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer benchmarks report 47–92% savings on several agent workloads. Tokbench independently verified 342K tokens removed on wire in an N=1 pilot, but the run still billed 43% more input than native because it took more turns.
repositories.main_caveat: Verified per-request compression can be outweighed by longer execution paths. Compression fidelity, cache behavior, and total turns must be measured on the target workload; Tokbench replication was still pending. Fresh pinned source-logic inspection is available; benchmark-audit and reproduction remain required before measured savings or deployment-grade recommendation.

repositories.name: kompact
repositories.summary: A transparent LLM API proxy with schema, JSON, code, log, history, and cache-alignment transforms.
repositories.mechanism: A transparent LLM API proxy with schema, JSON, code, log, history, and cache-alignment transforms.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer reports 40–70% token-bill reduction, with BFCL and other dataset scripts included for compression and quality checks.
repositories.main_caveat: Compression can alter tool schemas or code semantics; per-transform quality should be tested on the target workflow.

repositories.name: pctx
repositories.summary: Code Mode executes multi-tool MCP workflows inside a sandbox and returns only selected program output instead of placing every intermediate result in context.
repositories.mechanism: Code Mode executes multi-tool MCP workflows inside a sandbox and returns only selected program output instead of placing every intermediate result in context.
repositories.reported_result: README demonstrates a 150k-to-2k token multi-step example, described as a 98.7% reduction.
repositories.main_caveat: The headline result is a worked example, not a broad coding benchmark; generated sandbox code adds a security and correctness boundary. Fresh pinned source-logic inspection is available; benchmark-audit and reproduction remain required before measured savings or deployment-grade recommendation.

repositories.name: ast-grep
repositories.summary: AST-aware structural search and rewriting that can return exact code matches without broad file reads.
repositories.mechanism: AST-aware structural search and rewriting that can return exact code matches without broad file reads.
repositories.reported_result: agentic-token-bench reports 93.3% reduction on its pinned ast-grep tasks.
repositories.main_caveat: Rules are syntax- and language-specific; incorrect patterns can miss relevant code or rewrite unintended nodes.

repositories.name: ripgrep
repositories.summary: Fast, selective text and file search that lets an agent retrieve matching paths or lines instead of reading entire directories.
repositories.mechanism: Fast, selective text and file search that lets an agent retrieve matching paths or lines instead of reading entire directories.
repositories.reported_result: agentic-token-bench reports 95.4% reduction on its pinned ripgrep tasks.
repositories.main_caveat: A general CLI, not an agent-aware optimizer; poor query construction can still produce large or misleading output.

repositories.name: comby
repositories.summary: Language-aware structural search and replacement that can produce concise match or diff output for agents.
repositories.mechanism: Language-aware structural search and replacement that can produce concise match or diff output for agents.
repositories.reported_result: agentic-token-bench reports 83.6% reduction on its pinned Comby tasks.
repositories.main_caveat: A general transformation tool; token savings depend on agents using targeted templates instead of reading full files.

repositories.name: fastmod
repositories.summary: Fast, interactive search-and-replace/codemod tool that can apply broad edits without sending every affected file through the model.
repositories.mechanism: Fast, interactive search-and-replace/codemod tool that can apply broad edits without sending every affected file through the model.
repositories.reported_result: agentic-token-bench reports 65.1% reduction on its pinned fastmod tasks.
repositories.main_caveat: Best for mechanically specified replacements; agents must still inspect semantic changes and tests.

repositories.name: cavemem
repositories.summary: Cross-agent local memory that captures session observations, deterministically compresses prose at rest, and exposes progressive search, timeline, and full-body retrieval through MCP.
repositories.mechanism: Cross-agent local memory that captures session observations, deterministically compresses prose at rest, and exposes progressive search, timeline, and full-body retrieval through MCP.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer reports roughly 75% fewer prose tokens in stored observations, with code blocks, paths, URLs, identifiers, and versions preserved.
repositories.main_caveat: At-rest compression is not the same as provider-billed savings; memory capture, embeddings, retrieval quality, and reinjection policy determine the net effect. Fresh pinned source-logic inspection is available; benchmark-audit and reproduction remain required before measured savings or deployment-grade recommendation.

repositories.name: token-savior
repositories.summary: Combines symbol-level code navigation, persistent memory, compact MCP manifests, Bash command rewriting, and output compactors.
repositories.mechanism: Combines symbol-level code navigation, persistent memory, compact MCP manifests, Bash command rewriting, and output compactors.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer reports about 80% fewer active tokens per task on a 96-task tsbench run, with benchmark fixtures published separately.
repositories.main_caveat: Results are maintainer-run and profile-dependent; the tool exposes many features that can add overhead when poorly configured.

repositories.name: context-mode
repositories.summary: An MCP and hook layer that executes heavy analysis in sandboxes, indexes session events and large artifacts in SQLite/FTS5, and returns only selected results to the model context.
repositories.mechanism: An MCP and hook layer that executes heavy analysis in sandboxes, indexes session events and large artifacts in SQLite/FTS5, and returns only selected results to the model context.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer examples report 315 KB reduced to 5.4 KB and 47 file reads totaling about 700 KB replaced by one 3.6 KB execution result.
repositories.main_caveat: The examples are not a neutral end-to-end benchmark. Generated analysis code and routing rules introduce correctness and sandbox boundaries; the repository uses Elastic License 2.0 rather than an OSI-approved license. Fresh pinned source-logic inspection is available; benchmark-audit and reproduction remain required before measured savings or deployment-grade recommendation.

repositories.name: lean-ctx
repositories.summary: A local Rust context-intelligence layer combining cached and AST-aware file reads, shell-output compression, adaptive routing, persistent memory, a code graph, budgets, and an auditable savings ledger.
repositories.mechanism: A local Rust context-intelligence layer combining cached and AST-aware file reads, shell-output compression, adaptive routing, persistent memory, a code graph, budgets, and an auditable savings ledger.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer reports 60–90% fewer tokens for reads and shell output and cached rereads near 13 tokens. In Tokbench's N=1 external pilot, provider-billed input was 38% above native in MCP mode and 59% above native with the default integration.
repositories.main_caveat: The product covers many mechanisms, but end-to-end savings depend on whether agents actually use the optimized surfaces and whether additional tool calls increase total turns. The external benchmark is configuration-specific and single-run. Fresh pinned source-logic inspection is available; benchmark-audit and reproduction remain required before measured savings or deployment-grade recommendation.

repositories.name: ccusage
repositories.summary: Reads local coding-agent logs and reports token use, cache tokens, models, sessions, billing windows, and estimated costs.
repositories.mechanism: Reads local coding-agent logs and reports token use, cache tokens, models, sessions, billing windows, and estimated costs.
repositories.reported_result: No automatic saving mechanism; enables measurement and regression tracking across many coding agents.
repositories.main_caveat: Cost estimates depend on pricing data and the completeness of local logs.

repositories.name: tokbench
repositories.summary: An independent, transcript-preserving benchmark for token-saving middleware that compares provider-billed usage, product self-metrics, latency, and quality on a long-running software-engineering workflow.
repositories.mechanism: An independent, transcript-preserving benchmark for token-saving middleware that compares provider-billed usage, product self-metrics, latency, and quality on a long-running software-engineering workflow.
repositories.reported_result: Its N=1 pilot found all tested middleware arms billed more input tokens than native on a context-frugal harness, even though Headroom verifiably removed 342K tokens on wire; multi-run replication was pending.
repositories.main_caveat: The harness author discloses product conflicts, the pilot uses one task and provider, and single-run total differences cannot establish general performance; its main value is methodology and counter-evidence.

repositories.name: abacus
repositories.summary: Team dashboard for AI coding-tool token consumption, cost, model breakdown, users, and provider synchronization.
repositories.mechanism: Team dashboard for AI coding-tool token consumption, cost, model breakdown, users, and provider synchronization.
repositories.reported_result: No automatic token reduction; intended for organizational visibility and policy decisions.
repositories.main_caveat: Requires administrative APIs, a database, and access controls appropriate for team usage data.

repositories.name: abtop
repositories.summary: A read-only TUI for live coding-agent sessions, token usage, context-window fill, rate limits, child processes, and ports.
repositories.mechanism: A read-only TUI for live coding-agent sessions, token usage, context-window fill, rate limits, child processes, and ports.
repositories.reported_result: No automatic token reduction; provides live signals for deciding when to compact, stop, or reconfigure sessions.
repositories.main_caveat: Monitoring by itself does not establish causality or reduce context.

repositories.name: splitrail
repositories.summary: Cross-platform token-usage and cost tracker for multiple coding agents, with CLI, VS Code, cloud aggregation, and MCP query tools.
repositories.mechanism: Cross-platform token-usage and cost tracker for multiple coding agents, with CLI, VS Code, cloud aggregation, and MCP query tools.
repositories.reported_result: No automatic saving mechanism; supports comparative usage analysis across tools.
repositories.main_caveat: Optional cloud upload changes the privacy model; keep auto-upload disabled when local-only handling is required.

repositories.name: agentic-token-bench
repositories.summary: A deterministic benchmark and installer that measures before/after tokens and quality for CLI tools used in coding-agent workflows.
repositories.mechanism: A deterministic benchmark and installer that measures before/after tokens and quality for CLI tools used in coding-agent workflows.
repositories.reported_result: Pinned Cassandra tasks report 65.1–99.2% reductions for six tools, with exact validators and a second quality-retention layer.
repositories.main_caveat: Task-level artifact reduction is not the same as end-to-end session savings; workloads and agent behavior differ.

repositories.name: tokentop
repositories.summary: Real-time local dashboard for provider and coding-agent token use, burn rate, budgets, cache leverage, and project-level costs.
repositories.mechanism: Real-time local dashboard for provider and coding-agent token use, burn rate, budgets, cache leverage, and project-level costs.
repositories.reported_result: No automatic saving mechanism; supplies budget guardrails and efficiency diagnostics.
repositories.main_caveat: Provider APIs and locally discovered credentials can expose sensitive metadata; review storage and access controls.

repositories.name: gitingest
repositories.summary: Turns a local or remote Git repository into a prompt-friendly digest with file-tree, size, and token statistics.
repositories.mechanism: Turns a local or remote Git repository into a prompt-friendly digest with file-tree, size, and token statistics.
repositories.reported_result: No compression benchmark was reviewed; its value is selective, reproducible repository ingestion and token accounting.
repositories.main_caveat: A digest is not automatically minimal; users must exclude generated, vendored, secret, and irrelevant files. Fresh pinned source-logic inspection is available; benchmark-audit and reproduction remain required before measured savings or deployment-grade recommendation.

repositories.name: repomix
repositories.summary: Packs repositories into AI-friendly files with token counts, include/exclude controls, and Tree-sitter code compression.
repositories.mechanism: Packs repositories into AI-friendly files with token counts, include/exclude controls, and Tree-sitter code compression.
repositories.reported_result: No universal reduction percentage was reviewed; the --compress mode extracts key code elements to reduce token count.
repositories.main_caveat: Packing an entire repository can increase context use; aggressive filtering and compression are essential. Fresh pinned source-logic inspection is available; benchmark-audit and reproduction remain required before measured savings or deployment-grade recommendation.

repositories.name: minified-state-in-context-agent
repositories.summary: Research implementation of a direct-solve SWE-bench agent that minifies codebase state and compares file-ranking encodings and repair outcomes.
repositories.mechanism: Research implementation of a direct-solve SWE-bench agent that minifies codebase state and compares file-ranking encodings and repair outcomes.
repositories.reported_result: The associated paper reports substantial input-token reduction but also a lower issue-resolution rate, illustrating the quality trade-off.
repositories.main_caveat: A research prototype, not a production plugin; reproduce against the pinned datasets and models before drawing conclusions.

repositories.name: swe-pruner
repositories.summary: Task-aware context pruning for coding agents: a lightweight neural skimmer scores code tokens/lines against a query and exposes local service plus agent wrappers for pruning source, file, and command-output context.
repositories.mechanism: A local `swe-pruner` service accepts `{query, code}`, scores token/line relevance with a Qwen-reranker-derived model, emits pruned code with filtered-line markers and token-count fields, and can be wired into Claude/OpenHands/mini-swe-agent loops through wrapper tools.
repositories.reported_result: README/research claims include large token reductions, but this repository does not accept the tool as an evaluation candidate because basic operation depends on heavyweight local neural-model runtime/model files and likely GPU-class infrastructure.
repositories.main_caveat: Evaluation-ineligible for this program: GPU/heavyweight model-runtime dependencies are outside the practical candidate boundary; preserve as a rejected research note only, not a benchmark-audit/reproduction target.

candidate_decision.reason: Requires heavyweight local neural-model runtime/model files and likely GPU-class infrastructure for basic service operation; this eval program does not evaluate GPU-demanding systems.

repositories.name: cavegemma
repositories.summary: A Gemma 4 31B QLoRA fine-tune that bakes terse technical output into model weights so no recurring brevity system prompt is required.
repositories.mechanism: A Gemma 4 31B QLoRA fine-tune that bakes terse technical output into model weights so no recurring brevity system prompt is required.
repositories.reported_result: On a 193-pair holdout, the maintainer reports about 65% compression, 91–98% semantic similarity by category, and 96–100% exact preservation of source code fences.
repositories.main_caveat: The evaluation is style and semantic-similarity oriented rather than a coding-task benchmark; a 31B model has substantial hardware requirements and Gemma license terms apply to the weights.

repositories.name: LLMLingua

repositories.mechanism: Model-based prompt compression that removes lower-importance tokens, with LLMLingua, LongLLMLingua, and LLMLingua-2 implementations.
repositories.reported_result: Project reports up to 20× compression in research settings, with task-dependent quality retention.
repositories.main_caveat: Not coding-agent-specific; code, JSON, and tool schemas can be brittle under learned token deletion and require dedicated evaluation.

repositories.name: compression-layer
repositories.summary: Trains small-model LoRA adapters to rewrite verbose context into shorter representations and evaluates downstream equivalence.
repositories.mechanism: Trains small-model LoRA adapters to rewrite verbose context into shorter representations and evaluates downstream equivalence.
repositories.reported_result: Adapters reached roughly 35–39% output/input token ratios, but the published DS1000 results show large code-generation quality losses for aggressive learned compression.
repositories.main_caveat: Useful as a cautionary benchmark: compression ratio alone is not evidence that coding quality is preserved.

repositories.name: skim
repositories.summary: AST-aware code skimming plus command rewriting and compactors for test, build, lint, package-manager, and Git output.
repositories.mechanism: AST-aware code skimming plus command rewriting and compactors for test, build, lint, package-manager, and Git output.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer examples show code transformation modes ranging from light cleanup to roughly 90–95% reduction for signatures or types.
repositories.main_caveat: Aggressive structural modes deliberately omit implementations and are unsuitable when exact behavior is required.

repositories.name: trs
repositories.summary: A native token-reducing shell that parses command output, rewrites supported commands, provides compact file/search tools, builds budgeted project digests, and can install an output-saver rules block.
repositories.mechanism: A native token-reducing shell that parses command output, rewrites supported commands, provides compact file/search tools, builds budgeted project digests, and can install an output-saver rules block.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer examples report 76% reduction for git status, 90% for cargo clippy, and 99% for an all-passing cargo test output; unsupported commands receive generic cleanup.
repositories.main_caveat: Examples are command-level reductions rather than an end-to-end coding-task benchmark, and parser coverage varies by command and platform.

repositories.name: xcsift

repositories.mechanism: Parses Xcode and Swift Package Manager build/test output into concise JSON, TOON, or GitHub Actions formats for coding agents.

repositories.main_caveat: Out of current Codex token-optimization candidate scope: specialized Apple/Xcode output parser requiring Apple/Xcode fixtures and host support.

repositories.name: mcp-trim

repositories.name: rtk
repositories.summary: A Rust CLI proxy that filters and compresses shell, Git, test, build, package-manager, and other command output before it enters an agent context.
repositories.mechanism: A Rust CLI proxy that filters and compresses shell, Git, test, build, package-manager, and other command output before it enters an agent context.
repositories.reported_result: Maintainer reports roughly 60–90% reduction for supported command output. Tokbench independently observed 74.7% reduction on commands RTK touched, but those commands represented only about 2.5% of total spend in its N=1 pilot and the full run billed 27% more input tokens than native.
repositories.main_caveat: Operation-level compression does not guarantee lower task-level billing; command coverage, turn count, prompt caching, and harness design determine the addressable surface. The external result is a single-run pilot.
